gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states how many 8-hour days each sub-$100 low-profile board runs per charge on its maker's rating: about 9 for the Keychron K3 Max ChatGPT picked (73 h), 12.5 for the Lofree Flow Lite 2 84 (100 h), about 69 for the $98.99 Keychron K3 Ultra 8K (550 h) and 125 for the NuPhy Node75 low-profile (1,000 h).
standout_why: Compared against pcreviewer.org (cited), kbdcompare.com (cited) and rtings.com. pcreviewer already does the hours ÷ 8 sum, but only for the K3 Pro (8.5 days backlit, 16 days unlit); it lists raw hours for the K3 Max (78 h), Air75 V2 (220 h) and Flow Lite 84 (about 80 h), gives no prices, and never mentions the K3 Ultra 8K or Node75. kbdcompare gives K3 Pro hours (100 h off, 50 h RGB) and prices but no per-charge figure. rtings' list page carries no battery numbers. So rivals have the method for one board; the cross-board spread at today's prices and the K3 Ultra 8K are new. Two cited pages could not be opened (purchase.fyi: certificate error; technobezz.com: HTTP 403), so the score is 2 against the pages read, not all of them.
decides: It splits the pick by how often the shopper will charge. ChatGPT's top pick, the K3 Max, has the shortest rating of the wireless 75% boards read (73 h, about 9 workdays). For $26.50 more, the K3 Ultra 8K is still under the line at $98.99 and Keychron rates it 7.5 times longer on a cell only 1.68 times bigger. Our Lofree Flow Lite 2 84 (100 h, 12.5 workdays) beats the K3 Max on rated runtime but not the K3 Max SE (15), K3 Ultra 8K or Node75, so it should win its row on gasket mount and typing feel, not battery. All ratings are makers' 'up to' figures; the backlight condition was not on the store text read, so the page must say so.

findings.value: 7.5× the hours on a 1.68× cell; implied draw 4.7 mA vs 21.2 mA

findings.note: 550 ÷ 73 = 7.5; 2,600 ÷ 1,550 = 1.68; 2,600 mAh ÷ 550 h = 4.7 mA. Most of the gain is lower draw, not capacity. Costs $98.99 − $72.49 = $26.50 more than the K3 Max for 477 more rated hours.
